purpose: Shared ship and weapon art assembly contract; not gameplay socket or balance specification

coordinates.units: relative design units; no meters implied
coordinates.weaponScale: uniform per assembly, recorded explicitly; do not rescale the hull

ownership.shipDesigner: ship silhouette, candidate mount space and structural load path
ownership.weaponDesigner: weapon body, mount datum, facing and moving-part clearance

assemblyRecordsRequired: weapon-local mount datum and forward axis
static clearance observations and unresolved movement clearance
artRules: Retain the selected ship silhouette and cream balloon, honey wood, teal machinery, brass and coral accents
Create an attached structural path using fitted wood saddles, brass brackets and deliberate pipes or cables
Avoid standalone showroom plinths visibly resting on the ship; hide or adapt them in the assembly without changing original assets
Give one primary machine visual emphasis and make added weapons subordinate where the branch already has a primary machine
Keep cockpit, balloon silhouette, propulsion and branch-defining devices readable
Mobility: low, close mounting; preserve gliding panels and propulsion clearance
Artillery: connect added weapon supports to existing gun deck and recoil structure; avoid obscuring the primary gun
Salvage: keep recovery dock and cargo path visibly open; place auxiliary weapons off that path
Match material brightness, grain impression and outline treatment in one runtime

review.deliverables: 3 actual assembled GLBs, offline before/after comparison viewer, PNGs, placement records
review.comparison: same camera, same ship scale, same lighting; bare latest ship versus assembled ship
review.limitations: Art placement prototype. No engine sockets, physics, aiming, firing, damage, save changes or gameplay load validation implied.
